description: Practical decision techniques linked to reviewed cognitive-bias lenses. They are structured checks, not guaranteed cures.

techniques.title: Consider the opposite
techniques.purpose: Force a preferred explanation to compete with a credible alternative.
techniques.whenToUse: When evidence collection is drifting toward support for one preferred conclusion.
steps: Write the current conclusion in one sentence.
Write the strongest plausible alternative.
List evidence that would be more likely if the alternative were true.
Search for or request that evidence before finalizing the decision.
techniques.limitations: A weak straw-man alternative adds little value. The alternative must be genuinely plausible.

techniques.title: Independent estimate before the anchor
techniques.purpose: Create a reference point before seeing a strong external number or recommendation.
techniques.whenToUse: Before estimates, negotiations, AI recommendations or expert forecasts where the first number may become an anchor.
steps: Hide or postpone the external estimate when practical.
Write your own estimate or range and assumptions.
Then inspect the external number.
Record why your estimate changed, if it changed.
techniques.limitations: Independent estimates can still be poor; use reference classes and evidence when available.

techniques.title: Reference-class forecasting
techniques.purpose: Use outcomes from comparable completed cases before refining an inside-view plan.
techniques.whenToUse: For schedules, budgets, adoption forecasts and other repeatable predictions.
steps: Define the decision or quantity to forecast.
Find a meaningful set of comparable completed cases.
Use their distribution to set a baseline range.
Adjust only for specific differences that can be defended with evidence.
techniques.limitations: A bad comparison class can mislead. Similarity must be argued, not assumed.

techniques.title: Base-rate check
techniques.purpose: Compare a vivid case with the broader frequency or distribution that should inform the judgment.
techniques.whenToUse: When one story, recent event or exceptional example is carrying too much weight.
steps: State the event or outcome you are judging.
Find the relevant denominator or broader comparison set.
Estimate the base rate before focusing on case-specific details.
Explain what case evidence is strong enough to move away from that baseline.
techniques.limitations: Base rates can be irrelevant if the comparison population is badly chosen.

techniques.title: Decision journal
techniques.purpose: Preserve what was known, expected and uncertain before the outcome changes memory.
techniques.whenToUse: For important forecasts, project decisions, incident reviews and repeated professional judgments.
steps: Record the decision and date.
Record evidence, assumptions and uncertainty.
Write what would change the decision.
Review the original record after the outcome before drawing lessons.
techniques.limitations: A journal improves learning only if it is written before the result and revisited later.

techniques.title: Red-team review
techniques.purpose: Give a strong alternative case enough space to challenge the preferred option.
techniques.whenToUse: Before approvals, vendor selection, roadmap commitments and consequential group decisions.
steps: State the current preferred option and its strongest argument.
Assign a reviewer to build the best case against it.
Require concrete failure modes and missing evidence, not generic criticism.
Resolve or explicitly accept the strongest remaining uncertainty before approval.
techniques.limitations: A ritual adversarial review can become theatre. The red team needs access to evidence and permission to change the decision.

techniques.title: Predefined update criteria
techniques.purpose: Decide in advance what evidence should cause a forecast or decision to change.
techniques.whenToUse: When teams may later reinterpret evidence to preserve a public commitment.
steps: Write the current decision or forecast.
List observable evidence that would strengthen it.
List observable evidence that would weaken or stop it.
Set a review point before the evidence arrives.
techniques.limitations: Criteria should be revisable when the environment changes, but revisions should be recorded rather than silently rewritten.

techniques.title: Incremental-value check
techniques.purpose: Evaluate the next step using future cost and value rather than resources already spent.
techniques.whenToUse: When a project, product or career path continues mainly because of past investment.
steps: Write what has already been spent and mark it as unrecoverable.
Estimate the future cost of the next step.
Estimate the future value and uncertainty of the next step.
Ask whether you would fund that next step if the project arrived today with no history.
techniques.limitations: Past investment can contain useful information about capability or switching cost; ignore sunk cost, not relevant future consequences.

techniques.title: Predefined decision criteria
techniques.purpose: Fix the comparison dimensions before a preferred option makes the criteria move.
techniques.whenToUse: Hiring, vendor selection, product prioritization, career choices and evaluations.
steps: Write the decision goal.
Choose a small set of criteria before reviewing options.
Define how evidence maps to each criterion.
Score or discuss all serious options using the same criteria before adding exceptions.
techniques.limitations: Criteria can omit important information. Allow explicit revisions, but record why the criteria changed.

techniques.title: Source trace
techniques.purpose: Separate independent evidence from repetition and generated summaries.
techniques.whenToUse: When a claim appears in many articles, AI answers or internal documents.
steps: Write the exact claim.
Trace each important mention back to its earliest inspectable source.
Group copies that depend on the same origin.
Judge confidence from independent evidence, not the number of repetitions.
techniques.limitations: The earliest source is not automatically the best source; quality and methodology still matter.

techniques.title: Small reversible test
techniques.purpose: Reduce uncertainty before making a large commitment that is expensive to reverse.
techniques.whenToUse: When a career, product or operating decision can be partially tested before full commitment.
steps: Name the uncertainty that matters most.
Design the smallest action that produces relevant evidence.
Define the result that would change the larger decision.
Run the test and update the decision using the predefined rule.
techniques.limitations: A small test may not represent full-scale conditions. Treat it as evidence, not proof.
